title: Recursive Integer Power
description: Read two integers a and b and print a raised to the power b (a**b), computed with a RECURSIVE function: any number to the power 0 is 1, otherwise it is a times the power for b - 1. The base case is on the EXPONENT, and every call must shrink it toward zero. This is the transfer variant of 'Recursive Factorial': same C8 skill (reachable base case plus progress toward it), different decomposition shape. Reusing the single-argument factorial recursion cannot process the two-argument power inputs.
constraints: Input is two integers separated by a space.
starter_code:
def power(a, b):
    """Return a**b recursively."""
    # TODO: handle the base case (b == 0) then recurse on b - 1
    raise NotImplementedError


def main():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return
    a = int(data[0])
    b = int(data[1])
    print(power(a, b))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
input_format: Two integers a and b separated by a space.
output_format: A single integer: a raised to the power b.
